Source-traced failure, not an observed retail-frame failure: FrontendSession::create (src/app/FrontendSession.cpp:11-86) has no flags input and completionFlags_ (FrontendSession.h:100) starts all-zero; completeLevel (:222-250) and confirmChoice(yes) (:95-106) only mutate memory; main.cpp help says 'no save writes'; src/shell/Progress.* has no production caller. This is the earliest unparked dependency of the restart step; save-research-001 (done) supplies the contract in docs/scratch/save-format-research.md sections 4-7 and 10-11. Read it first.

Persistence contract (explicit, not a claim of retail compatibility). Format: the reader at 0x45F43C and writer at 0x45F94D, exe SHA-256 32675bdb49866e76502713251fdfd2b09078c2481c72ca22ff68ebf4b3737a2f. File layout: int32 LE flag at 0x000, then for n=group*25+slot (5x25 records) A, B, C int32 LE at 0x004+12n+{0,4,8}, total 1504 bytes. Storage: the clone's own copy at %LOCALAPPDATA%\LemmingsWebolution\SavedGame.dat via a Windows adapter, plus an injected-path constructor for tests and a future web store. Never read-modify or write the installed 'Lemmings Revolution/SavedGame.dat'. Do not silently import it, and do not use the WEBOPROG model or Progress::complete unlock rule. Caveat to record: the installed sample is all zero, so it confirms size and the zero state only; nonzero field positions rest on disassembly, not on a sample. Evidence: reading the installed save and reference exe as static data is authorized; no original execution, hooks, debugger, capture or oracle runner.

Implement, in this order:
1. Mapping (blocks wiring). Verify read-only, by a source test that first hashes the exe and compares it to the registered SHA-256, that the 102 12-byte entries at VA 0x4B3948 (file offset 0xB3948, size 1224; {int group, int slot, byte base}) equal the clone's MapScene kMapping (src/app/MapScene.cpp:47-150) entry-for-entry. This resolves research item U3. If it disagrees, STOP and report the exact per-node differences as a blocker instead of editing either table. Then expose the mapping from MapScene as a public accessor; do not duplicate the table and do not change MapScene::build behavior.
2. Pure codec (new src/save/SavedGame.{h,cpp}, no I/O): SavedGame{flagRaw, 125 x {A,B,C raw int32}}; parse(span) requires exactly 1504 bytes and returns std::expected with a specific error (the original reads short files as indeterminate stack data and ignores oversize files; rejecting both is a documented deliberate clone policy); serialize() emits 1504 bytes little-endian independent of host endianness; flag, A, B, all 23 unmapped records and nonzero C values are kept verbatim (document that the original would normalise flag to 0/1 on rewrite). Helpers: set C=1 for a (group,slot); project C != 0 into the 102-node flags and merge flags back by (group,slot).
3. Storage adapter (new src/save/SaveStore.{h,cpp}, separate from the codec): resolve LocalAppData (SHGetKnownFolderPath or LOCALAPPDATA) behind a small interface, create the directory, load (missing file -> zero state, matching the original open-fails path; wrong size or unreadable -> error, the file is never overwritten by a failed load), and save by writing a temp file in the same directory then atomically replacing (MoveFileExW REPLACE_EXISTING or std::filesystem equivalent) so that on any failure the prior good file is kept and an error is returned. Refuse any resolved target inside the installed game directory (the --game-dir / WEBOLUTION_GAME_DIR tree). Keep the storage interface injectable so a failing sink and temp-directory paths can be tested.
4. Integration (minimal, no new gameplay or menu rule): FrontendSession::create takes an optional store. On create it loads and seeds completionFlags_, map_ and initialMap_ rebuilt via MapScene::build with the loaded flags. The session's reset target for New Game stays the zero-flag map, so confirmChoice(yes) must restore a zero-flag map, not the loaded one. A corrupt or short file leaves the session empty with a visible stderr diagnostic and is never overwritten until a successful save of a new state replaces it; decide and document this in the note. After the in-memory commit, completeLevel saves when outcome.success (matching 0x485E55 mark-C-and-write); a failed save reports an error without discarding the on-screen results. New Game Yes writes the zero image to the clone path only (matches the 0x49BCF4/0x49BCFE reset-then-write), preserving unmapped-record data per the codec policy. No save on loss, retry, abandon or exit (matching the call graph). runApplication selects the default store; add an injectable store/path hook to ApplicationRunOptions (tests only) so no test touches the real LocalAppData. Existing asset-free tests must keep passing without writing anywhere, so the default for tests that do not opt in must not touch disk.
5. Update --help text and README to state where progress is stored and that the installed save is never read or written. Do not change docs/STATUS.md gate rows.

Out of scope: language/volume, meaning of A/B, flag semantics beyond preservation, Emscripten store, WEBOPROG removal, GUI save dialogs, audio, any change to level timing or rendering.

review_feedback.reason:
The extraction and most of the static work are strong, but two critical frame-state dependencies were left untraced. The task must be revised, not accepted, and not marked blocked.

What holds up:
- `scenebranch_measure` ran under the verifier. Main passed 93/93 and recovery 84/84.
- `records.txt` has real offsets, fields, names, parent/child structure and sprite metadata. It lists 86 nodes and 19 branch-1 nodes. The traversal ends exactly at 0xC3056, and there are no nested nodes.
- The `fire.SPR` resolution, the executable constants and the draw/blend/directional analysis are address-backed. The draw/blend/directional analysis shows that `0x46840B` returns early when there is only one directional image.

What fails:
1. The random first-frame state is not closed (gap 5).
   - The report says the `srand` seed values at the two call sites `0x4451E5` and `0x45D06C` "were not traced". The retained disassembly shows what they are.
   - Each call passes `fild` of the result of `0x4657D1` to the `srand` wrapper `0x447580`.
   - `0x4657D1` (disassembly lines 130442-130451) is `call [0x4B0220]` minus `[this+8]`. That is an elapsed value from an imported timer, and the report does not identify which import `0x4B0220` is.
   - The stated reason for leaving it open was "a general game-flow dependency", but it is a few instructions of available disassembly.
   - The contract then gives `CrtRand` a default state of 1 and a worked example from that state. That is a deterministic stand-in for what looks like clock-derived original state. The acceptance criteria forbid exactly this.
   - The report must identify the `0x4B0220` import, the owner of `[this+8]` (the base timestamp), when `srand` is called relative to the first scenery draw, and the units. It must then state the true policy, such as a clock-derived seed with tests injecting explicit state. Alternatively, it can establish that the start-of-play state is not reproducible.
2. The `dt` time unit for the temporal frame advance is untraced.
   - The report calls it "unverified" and "plausibly seconds", then has the contract take `dt` from the application's seconds clock.
   - That is a guess about a frame-timing semantic that the contract needs. The caller chain is `0x4764C4`, the owner's time double at `+0x120`/`+0x148`, and the setter `0x438F8A`. The report stopped at "reached only through a vtable".
   - It must find the vtable slot or callers that feed the time double and establish its unit and source, or state exactly why that is impossible.
3. Several inputs are carried as "inherited, unverified" rather than closed.
   - The vertex diffuse colour and the node tint at `node+0x340` for branch 1.
   - The shared `0x46D3C1` submit, which was not re-read.
   - The `0x58D53C` bracket (`0x441862..0x4419A0`) contents, so the assumed value of 0 on the main-view scenery route is unproven. It could stay a bounded limit only if its scope and the reason it is irrelevant to MM_DIG_000 are justified. They are not yet.
   - The vertex-orientation signs, deferred to a future test.
   - Together with items 1 and 2, these keep criterion 3 (no guessed critical semantics) and criterion 6 (no unread-but-available dependency presented as done) from being met.

The existing pieces are preserved. No production, controller or queue change, and no original execution, appears in the reports or the changed-file list. Keep the same task and finish items 1 and 2 first. Then resolve or properly bound items 3 and the diffuse and tint question.

Retained addresses: type-0 draw 0x0046B6CC, type-1 draw 0x0046C55D (visibility gate +0x110 at 0x46C56B; radius cull z+[this+0x100]<=0 at 0x46C5C4..0x46C5E4; own meshes then children in file order at 0x46C6F6..0x46C737), root slot+8 0x0046B73F (key = z'+child[+0x108], only direct children ordered), binary-insertion order 0x0046B8F4..0x0046BA72 with insert helper 0x0046C2A0. These are retained static findings.

Implementation (production):
1. SceneDispatch.{h,cpp}: add a function implementing the exact E10 binary-insertion ordering (descending by key; idx starts {0}; for i>=1: lo=0, hi=size-1; while(hi-lo>1){mid=(hi+lo)>>1; if(key[i]<key[idx[mid]]) lo=mid; else hi=mid;}; then if key[i]<key[idx[hi]] insert at hi+1, else if key[i]>key[idx[lo]] insert at lo, else insert at lo+1). Replace std::sort for the root's direct children with it. After each ordered direct child, emit its descendants depth-first in file order immediately after the child and before the next ordered child. Extend SecondaryDispatchItem with depth and parentOffset (additive; existing fields and existing callers keep compiling). Keys keep the existing formula. Do not order nested children.
2. Visibility: a node whose +0x110 is 0 emits nothing and its subtree is skipped. Type 0/1 default visible. Type-2 uses its serialized visibility byte (also for branch-0 billboards, which BackdropScene ignored; no installed level has a hidden type-2). The cutme frame-time LOD is NOT connected; cutme nodes stay visible and this is recorded as a limit.
3. Type-1 subtree cull: compute the camera-space depth z of the node origin (same quantity as the sort-key z before adding +0x108) and skip the node and its children if z + headDoubles[0] <= 0. Apply to every type-1 node as the original does. The ten originally admitted levels must stay byte-identical; if any other change appears there, restrict the rule to nodes with children, state the restriction, and report the exact evidence.
4. BackdropScene::build: replace the blanket nested/non-leaf guard with a structural predicate: Secondary root must be type 0 (unchanged); every node type 0, 1 or 2 (unchanged); a node may have children only if it is type 0 or type 1; a type-2 node with children keeps the existing 'unsupported ...' diagnostic (the double-matrix push at 0x47D0F2/0x46B6EB is evidenced but unexercised, so it is not implemented). No level-ID table, no marker scan, no per-level offsets. Keep admitSprites, buildSceneMeshSource/collectEyes (already nested-aware, keyed by nodeSourceOffset) and branch-1 behavior unchanged. Ensure nested mesh records are actually dispatched, and that billboard collection needs no change.
5. Preserve unchanged: SceneNode parsing, mesh/billboard builders, rasterizer arithmetic, SceneFrame schedule, camera, simulation, audio, saves, archive precedence, main.cpp (unless the demonstration needs a hook), and the Primary/LegacyUnattributed stages.

Edit limit: src/app/BackdropScene.{h,cpp}, src/app/SceneDispatch.{h,cpp}; tests and CMakeLists.txt registrations for bounded demonstrations.

review.reason: I checked the production code and the supervisor verification log against every criterion, and the executed results support all of them. I did not run anything and did not open the reference binary, so the E1–E11 binary addresses rest on the accepted scene-nested-research-001 report. Each ordered child is followed by its descendants depth-first in file order, with no reordering, and renderStage passes originalGates=true. Section 1.2 says there are no per-level timeline records to parse and that the list at 0x4CBF8C is not filled from the level file. That conclusion rests on a caller scan of 0x43F0C0, and two of the six callers (0x41527B and 0x456AF1) were never decompiled. When I decompiled them:

- **0x456AF1** (called only from 0x456733) is a `switch(*param_1)` over record types 0 to 9. It builds a 0x40-byte event via `FUN_00457260(obj, param_1[1])`, with `param_1[1]` as the time and type-specific payload fields. It then sets `obj[4] = type` and calls `FUN_0043f0c0(&DAT_004cbf8c, obj)`.
- **0x456733** (called only from 0x45651e) reads a counted record array from a stream at `this+0x18`. It calls `FUN_0047e40d` to open it, `FUN_00402560` for the count, and `FUN_00456a90` to parse each record, then hands each one to 0x456AF1.
- **0x41527B** has no resolved callers. It creates an event at `DAT_004cbf88 + 400`.

evidence.detail: `linkLevelGates` (lines 58-146) reads the structured gadget records. It builds `s.objectIds` in the traced loader collection order (later construction wins). It then calls `fanOutLeverLoadFaces`. Pairing a tagged record to its placed lever is by pose, which is a record-to-object association and not message dispatch. Dispatch itself is by serialized ID.

Establish from the installed animation data and static evidence which sequence and facing the original uses for the digger (and check whether any other state, such as blocker, shrugger or the explosion countdown, also uses a front-facing sequence the clone does not), and draw it so through the production actor path. Presentation only. Difficulty: routine. Recommended model: Sonnet. Playable v1, per agent/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and AGENTS.md 'Project lead direction'. Evidence of failure: the playtest ledgers under docs/playtest/. Use retained evidence and the static REA profile for what the original does; where static evidence is insufficient choose the simplest behavior that is correct for a player and label it provisional. No original execution, debugger, hooks or capture. Use a private temporary save path; never the installed or normal user save. No subagents or concurrent writers; no queue, verifier, controller or shared-instruction edits. Short report under docs/scratch/ with the production call path, limitations and a two-line handoff. Finish needs_review. Replay policy: a promoted recording that diverges only because of this task's intended fix does not block acceptance; name it with step and reason in the report and the lead retires it. Never edit, rename or weaken a recording or the replay check. Gate (AGENTS.md "Verification tiers"): the supervisor runs the smoke profile. Do not add before/after replay fixtures, frozen-source builds, identity checks or per-task scripted routes. The recorded human wins under docs/playtest/replays/ are the regression routes: run `webolution --game-dir "Lemmings Revolution" --replay <file>` on the ones for levels this change can affect and report each result; if an intended change makes one diverge, say why and leave the file alone. End the report with a what-to-check note: level, action, expected result.
acceptance: On Just Dig (MM_DIG_000) a digger faces the camera at every rotation while digging, and returns to its walking facing afterwards.
The sequence is cited to animation data or static evidence; any other front-facing state found is listed and either fixed the same way or reported.
All promoted playtest replays still reproduce their results.
The smoke profile passes and the report ends with a what-to-check note.

tasks.title: Pan and attenuate level sounds by where they happen on screen

UI sounds and the Let's Go voice stay centred.
